full_judgment:
15. The plaintiffs have come with an allegation that plaintiff. Nos.1-15 have acquired 12 annas 5 Gondas 1 Kora 1 Kranti share from disputed khatian by way of inheritance from R.S recorded tenant and plain-tiff No.16 acquired 3 annas 14 Gondas 2 Koras 2 Krantis share on basis of a settlement from Jagadish, one of the recorded tenants. The aforesaid RS Khatian has been prepared in the names of the plaintiffs which were marked as exhibit No.2 series and the same has been denied by the contesting defendants as per section 103-B of Bengal Tenancy Act, entries of the record have a unrebuttable presumptive value. The respondent failed to adduce any cogent evidence with a view to rebut the aforementioned presumption. From the plaint, it appears that Billuda Sundari Saha, Upendranath Saha, Jagadish Chandra Saha, Otul Chandra Saha, Boloram Saha, Lalon Chandra Saha, Derendrandra Nath Saha and Moindra Nath Saha were the owners of the suit land. The inheritance chart and sub-sequent devaluation as has furnished in the plaint has not been challenged by the defendant. Not only that, PW1, Amarandra Nath Saha deposed that Billuda Sundari died leaving behind two sons named Jagadish and Otul. He also deposed that Jagadish had 1 annas 1 Gonda 1 Kora 1 Kranti share and he inherited 2 annas 13 Gondas 1 Kora 1 Kranti share from his mother in the suit Khatian. There is no denial of the fact that plaintiff Nos.1-15 did not inherit the aforementioned share from the RS record tenant. 

 17. The case of the contesting defendants is that the suit land appertaining to 11/1, 11/2, 11/3, 11/4 numbers khabot under Khabot No.25 belongs to one Kader Nath Bhoumik which was put in auction and the interests of the tenancy were extinguished and one Puma Chandra Bhoumik took settlement of the same who stetted the suit land in the benami of mother's sister. It has been further alleged by the contesting defendant that Puma Chandra through patta 29.02.195.6 gave patta settlement in the benami of Nimpoma Datta and defendant No.1 claimed the suit and from his bemander and since then he has been pos-sessing the same. But the defendants failed to show any scrap of paper regarding such revenue sale or there was any assertion of such rent sale in the recital of such patta dated 29.02.1956. 

 18. Not only that, all rent receiving interest were acquired by Government under the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, before 1956AD and as a result of which, no title had been acquired by Nerupoma Datta by dint of patta date 29.02.1956 since the patta has been registered after 13.12.1955. Nor the defendant has been able to prove the fact that Nirupoma was the Benamder of the defendant consequently Profullya Kumar Sarker (defendant No.1) acquired no title over the suit land from Nerupoma Datta. Over and above, the defendants failed to record his name in the rent role Ichatian. Thus, we find that defendant No.1 miser-ably failed to prove his case. 

 "The defendant No.1 has failed to prove that the superior interest of the suit land was sold in revenue sale. There is no evidence that Ratikanta Saha again took settlement from the auction purchaser. There is no on record evidence that Ratikanta settled that suit land with Puma Chandra or his benamdar So, the title of Purnachandra has not been established by legal evidence. Defendant No.1 has stated that he took the suit land from Purnachandra by way of settlement by a register patta dated 29.02.1956 in the benami of his mother's sister Nirupama Datta. Alleged patta has marked Ext. Grha' settlement in the benami of Nirupama has not been proved by supporting evi-dence. All the rent-receiving interest were Acquisition and Tenancy Act before 1956AD. So, the alleged trans-fer by a registered patta dated 29.02.56 did not give any title to Nirupama Datta. If Nirupama Datta does not acquire title over the suit land by the said patta, how her sister's son Profulla Kumar Sarkar will acquire title over the suit land by way of inheritance. There is no description in the alleged patta that Purnachandra Saha or his predecessor purchased that land by auction. So, it has not been proved that the suit land was sold out by auction. According to law, no patta deed can be registered in the year, 1956AD and as such, no title can be passed by such a deed."
